title: Public Value and the BBC
content:
The BBC is under constant pressure to prove its value, and, like many other public institutions, it is viewed through a market-failure lens that limits its role to addressing gaps left by the private sector. It is also measured and evaluated by static, price-focused metrics that fail to capture outcomes that accumulate over time. That pressure is now coming to a head. Before the end of the year, the government will publish its White Paper on the BBC Charter Review, setting out its decisions on how the BBC will be funded, what its mission should be and which public purposes it should serve from 2028. How the BBC’s value is defined and measured will sit at the heart of those decisions.

Subscribe now

The Director-General of the BBC, Matt Brittin has the opportunity to re-shape and re-open the conversation surrounding value creation at the BBC. However, this conversation needs to start in the right way. That requires policymakers and regulators to recognise the BBC’s contribution to the British media landscape.
